newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Visbeen group splits into forwarding/transport.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Visbeen group splits into forwarding/transport.

text.p: The Visbeen Group has split into two separate companies in a bid to have a clearly differ its forwarding and transport activities, owner and director, Wim Visbeen said.

"This clarifies our business to our customers. Both forwarding and transport were expanding rapidly, especially the transport division which is expanding in Eastern Europe so it was just a logical move."
Established in 1925, the group's two new companies will be named Visbeen Holding(the transport company) and VMV Holding(the forwarding business).
The group is mainly specialised in the fruit, vegetable and flower industry. In total, 180 people work for the company, 130 will now work on the transport side and 50 in the forwarding company.

Companies forming part of the Visbeen Holding include: Visbeen & Sons (the Netherlands), Visbeen International Plc (Colchester, Felixstowe and Harwich), Visbeen Eastern Europe (Moscow) and Visbeen Finland. These companies will concentrate on road transport and road-related logistic services.

While under VMV, are Quality Handling Holland and Visbeen Forwarding & Logistics. Several companies are placed under the new forwarding and logistics organisation including Visbeen International Air Services, Visbeen Road Cargo and Visbeen USA (Los Angeles) and the group's Heathrow operations.
Quality Handling deals with product treatment and pallet construction amongst other things, he said.
Visbeen Forwarding & Logistics is currently building a new 2000 sq m warehouse near Schiphol Airport which is set for completion in May.
